created .doctrina/intake.md

Bootstrap playbook — agent-executed (ADR 0005); the CLI does no interpretation.

Execute in order, in a single linear pass:

1. Read .doctrina/intake.md (raw intent) and .doctrina/product.md.

2. Fill every product.md section from the intake: Vision, Problem,
   Target users, Scope (in/out), Non-goals, Success criteria, and the
   Delivery order — name the ONE end-to-end walking skeleton to build
   and verify before fanning out (depth before breadth).
   One fact, one home — product.md holds vision, never requirements.

3. Derive the capability list: kebab-case, one per area of behaviour
   (e.g. auth, billing, reports). For each capability:
       doctrina spec new <capability>
   then replace the template placeholders in
   .doctrina/specs/<capability>/spec.md with EARS requirements derived
   from the intake (Ubiquitous / Event-driven / State-driven /
   Unwanted-behavior / Optional). Keep the two axes honest — leave
   Implementation: planned for what is not built yet; keep aspiration
   under ## Maturity → Future, not in EARS; write concrete Acceptance
   criteria, each [unverified] until a cited test proves it.

4. If the project spans services/front-ends, own the seams between
   them (port map, env, API/WS/event shapes) as a contract:
       doctrina contract new <name> → fill it → doctrina contract check

5. Record any architectural decision the intake forces (cite Evidence):
       doctrina decision new "<title>" → edit → doctrina decision accept <num>

6. Quality gates — fix everything they report before moving on:
       doctrina clarify --all
       doctrina validate
       doctrina coverage   (and doctrina verify --init to declare the build gate)
   If something in the intake is genuinely ambiguous, ask the user
   before assuming.

7. Mark the intake consumed: in .doctrina/intake.md flip
   "- **Status:** pending" to "- **Status:** converted".

8. doctrina next — follow the recommendation. Implementation then
   flows through doctrina work "<brief prompt>", one change at a time.
